message.content: Logistic regression is a statistical method used for predicting a binary outcome (e.g., yes/no, success/failure) based on one or more predictor variables. Unlike linear regression, which models a continuous outcome, logistic regression models the probability that a given input belongs to a particular class. The key idea is to use the logistic (sigmoid) function to map any real-valued number into the (0, 1) interval, interpreting the result as a probability. The model estimates coefficients for each predictor that maximize the likelihood of observing the given outcomes. Once fitted, the model can be used to classify new observations by comparing the predicted probability to a threshold (commonly 0.5).
